# Ocufuse

> Ocufuse is an eye health journal and eye games app on the web, with an iPhone app launching November 29, 2026. It offers 16 free browser games for screen breaks on ocufuse.com (no download, free with an email address, no account needed; list: https://ocufuse.com/games), visual games and guided eye exercises in the app (including companions for exercises clinicians give for lazy eye, strabismus and convergence insufficiency), comfort routines for eye strain, a daily log, optional eye photos and a Doctor Brief to share with an eye care professional. Ocufuse is not a medical device and does not diagnose or treat any condition. It is free to start; Ocufuse Plus costs $7.99 a month (3-day free trial), $49.99 a year (7-day free trial) or $119.99 once for Lifetime. Web app: https://app.ocufuse.com

## Product
- [Ocufuse: eye symptom journal, screen breaks and Doctor Brief](https://ocufuse.com/): Log how your eyes feel and keep dated eye photos for free, take screen breaks with eye games and a 20-20-20 timer, and share a Doctor Brief with Plus.
- [Ocufuse Doctor Brief: A Guide for Eye Care Clinicians](https://ocufuse.com/clinicians): For ophthalmologists, optometrists, orthoptists and GPs: what an Ocufuse Doctor Brief contains, how patients make it, and its limits.
- [Safety, intended use and eye warning signs](https://ocufuse.com/safety): What Ocufuse is for and what it is not for, plus the eye warning signs that need a doctor straight away, such as sudden vision loss or double vision.
- [Ocufuse Plus: Plans, Pricing and Free Trial](https://ocufuse.com/plus): Ocufuse Plus unlocks every eye game, your full history, all 24 guides and the Doctor Brief. $7.99 a month, $49.99 a year with a 7-day free trial, or $119.99 once.
- [Ocufuse for iPhone: eye journal and eye games app](https://ocufuse.com/app): Ocufuse for iPhone: a daily eye journal with a reminder, eye games for short breaks, and sync with the web app. Launching November 29, 2026. Join the waiting list.

## Free eye games
- [Visual Memory: a free tile sequence game](https://ocufuse.com/games/visual-memory): Watch tiles light up one after another, then tap them back in the same order. A free memory game for screen breaks, and each round adds one tile.
- [Free eye games you can play in your browser](https://ocufuse.com/games): 16 free browser games for screen breaks in eight categories: aim, sport, focus, calm, screen breaks, puzzles, kids and easy pace. No download.
- [Shade Hunt: find the odd tile, a free screen-break game](https://ocufuse.com/games/shade-hunt): Find the one tile in a different color. A free 60-second browser game for screen breaks: the grid grows as the shades get closer. Free with email.
- [Dot Chase: follow the dot, a free screen-break game](https://ocufuse.com/games/dot-chase): Follow the moving dot with your eyes and catch it when it changes colour. A free two-minute follow-the-dot game for screen breaks, on phone or computer.
- [Edge Spot: watch the edges, a free screen-break game](https://ocufuse.com/games/edge-spot): Keep your eyes on the centre cross and spot the diamond that flashes at the edges. A free centre and edges game for screen breaks, with six levels.

## Free tools
- [Free eye tools: break timer, monitor distance and more](https://ocufuse.com/tools): Free browser tools: a 20-20-20 timer, a monitor distance calculator, a text size calculator, eye appointment questions, eye games and eye journals.
- [20-20-20 timer: free screen break reminder](https://ocufuse.com/tools/screen-break-timer): A free 20-20-20 timer in your browser. Every 20 minutes it reminds you to look 20 feet away for 20 seconds, with a chime or a notification.
- [Monitor distance calculator: screen distance and height](https://ocufuse.com/tools/monitor-distance): Find your screen size by device, tape or bank card, then see the viewing distance and screen height that OSHA and Mayo Clinic suggest. Free, in your browser.
- [Text size calculator: how big should text be on screen?](https://ocufuse.com/tools/text-size): Find your screen size and viewing distance, then see how tall text should be, using the ANSI/HFES 100-2007 workstation standard. Free, in your browser.
- [Eye appointment checklist: questions to ask, what to bring](https://ocufuse.com/tools/appointment-questions): A free printable eye appointment checklist: what to bring, how to describe what you notice and questions to ask, with space for your own notes.
- [Eye photo journal: dated eye photos for your doctor](https://ocufuse.com/tools/eye-photo-journal): Take eye photos the same way each time, keep them dated next to your notes, and show them at your eye appointment. Free in the Ocufuse web app.
- [Eye symptom journal and tracker: log how your eyes feel](https://ocufuse.com/eye-tracking-journal): Log eye symptoms that come and go, with screen time, sleep, drops and optional photos, in a few taps a day. Free in the Ocufuse web app.

## Eye exercises
- [Eye exercises: what the research says and how to track them](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/): Do eye exercises improve vision? What eye exercises can and can't do, the techniques clinicians prescribe, what the research says, and how to log them.
- [Convergence insufficiency: symptoms, diagnosis and research](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/convergence-insufficiency): What convergence insufficiency is, its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, and what the CITT trial and Cochrane review found. A plain guide; treatment decisions are for your eye care professional.
- [Pencil push-ups and the Brock string explained](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/pencil-push-ups-brock-string): How pencil push-ups and the Brock string work, why clinicians prescribe them for convergence insufficiency, and what the CITT trial found.
- [The 20-20-20 rule and digital eye strain explained](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/20-20-20-rule): What the 20-20-20 rule is, how digital eye strain happens, what a 2022 study found about screen breaks, and simple screen setup tips from eye care experts.
- [Eye exercise myths: palming and the Bates method](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/myths): Can eye exercises replace glasses? What eye care organisations say about palming, the Bates method and eye exercises for dyslexia.
- [Eye exercise log: tracking prescribed exercises](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/exercise-log): What to record when doing prescribed eye exercises at home, a simple log format, and how to bring it to your orthoptist or optometrist.
- [Ejercicios oculares: qué dice la investigación](https://ocufuse.com/es/ejercicios-oculares/): ¿Los ejercicios oculares mejoran la vista? Lo que pueden y no pueden hacer, las técnicas que indican los profesionales y las pruebas del CITT y Cochrane.
- [Insuficiencia de convergencia: síntomas y diagnóstico](https://ocufuse.com/es/ejercicios-oculares/insuficiencia-de-convergencia): Qué es la insuficiencia de convergencia, sus síntomas, cómo se diagnostica y qué encontraron el ensayo CITT y la revisión Cochrane. Una guía sencilla; las decisiones de tratamiento corresponden a tu profesional de la visión.
- [Flexiones con lápiz y el cordón de Brock explicados](https://ocufuse.com/es/ejercicios-oculares/flexiones-con-lapiz-y-cordon-de-brock): Cómo funcionan las flexiones con lápiz y el cordón de Brock, por qué se indican para la insuficiencia de convergencia y qué encontró el ensayo CITT.
- [La regla 20-20-20 y la fatiga visual digital: ¿funciona?](https://ocufuse.com/es/ejercicios-oculares/regla-20-20-20): Qué es la regla 20-20-20, qué es la fatiga visual digital, qué encontró un estudio de 2022 sobre las pausas de pantalla y qué aconseja la AOA.
- [Mitos sobre ejercicios oculares: palming y método Bates](https://ocufuse.com/es/ejercicios-oculares/mitos): ¿Pueden los ejercicios oculares sustituir a las gafas? Lo que dicen las organizaciones de salud visual sobre el palming, el método Bates y la dislexia.
- [Registro de ejercicios oculares: anota los indicados](https://ocufuse.com/es/ejercicios-oculares/registro-de-ejercicios): Qué anotar al hacer en casa los ejercicios oculares indicados, un formato de registro sencillo y cómo llevarlo a tu ortoptista u optometrista.
- [Göz egzersizleri: araştırmalar ne diyor?](https://ocufuse.com/tr/goz-egzersizleri/): Göz egzersizleri görmeyi iyileştirir mi? Neleri yapıp neleri yapamadıkları, uzmanların önerdiği teknikler ve CITT ile Cochrane kanıtları.
- [Yakınsama yetmezliği: belirtiler, teşhis ve araştırmalar](https://ocufuse.com/tr/goz-egzersizleri/yakinsama-yetmezligi): Yakınsama yetmezliğinin ne olduğu, belirtileri, nasıl teşhis edildiği ve CITT çalışması ile Cochrane derlemesinin bulguları. Sade bir rehber; tedavi kararları göz sağlığı uzmanınıza aittir.
- [Kalem egzersizi ve Brock ipi nedir](https://ocufuse.com/tr/goz-egzersizleri/kalem-egzersizi-ve-brock-ipi): Kalem egzersizi ve Brock ipinin nasıl çalıştığı, uzmanların bunları yakınsama yetmezliği için neden önerdiği ve CITT çalışmasının bulguları.
- [20-20-20 kuralı ve dijital göz yorgunluğu: işe yarar mı?](https://ocufuse.com/tr/goz-egzersizleri/20-20-20-kurali): 20-20-20 kuralı nedir, dijital göz yorgunluğu nedir, 2022 tarihli bir çalışma ekran molaları hakkında ne buldu ve AOA'nın ekran önerileri.
- [Göz egzersizleri mitleri: palming, Bates yöntemi ve gözlük](https://ocufuse.com/tr/goz-egzersizleri/mitler): Göz egzersizleri gözlüğün yerini alabilir mi? Göz sağlığı kuruluşlarının palming, Bates yöntemi ve disleksi için göz egzersizleri hakkında söyledikleri.
- [Göz egzersizi kaydı: önerilen egzersizleri takip edin](https://ocufuse.com/tr/goz-egzersizleri/egzersiz-kaydi): Önerilen göz egzersizlerini evde yaparken neleri kaydetmeli, basit bir kayıt formatı ve bunu ortoptistinize veya optometristinize nasıl götürmeli.
- [Ushtrimet e syve: çfarë thotë kërkimi dhe si t'i ndjekësh](https://ocufuse.com/sq/ushtrime-per-syte/): A e përmirësojnë shikimin ushtrimet e syve? Çfarë mund dhe nuk mund të bëjnë, teknikat që përshkruajnë profesionistët dhe provat e CITT dhe Cochrane.
- [Pamjaftueshmëria e konvergjencës: simptomat dhe diagnoza](https://ocufuse.com/sq/ushtrime-per-syte/pamjaftueshmeria-e-konvergjences): Çfarë është pamjaftueshmëria e konvergjencës, simptomat, si diagnostikohet dhe çfarë gjetën studimi CITT dhe rishikimi Cochrane. Udhëzues i thjeshtë; vendimet për trajtimin i merr profesionisti i syve.
- [Afrimi i lapsit dhe fija e Brock-ut të shpjeguara](https://ocufuse.com/sq/ushtrime-per-syte/afrimi-i-lapsit-dhe-fija-e-brockut): Si funksionojnë afrimi i lapsit dhe fija e Brock-ut, pse profesionistët i përshkruajnë për pamjaftueshmërinë e konvergjencës dhe çfarë gjeti studimi CITT.
- [Rregulli 20-20-20 dhe lodhja digjitale e syve: a funksionon?](https://ocufuse.com/sq/ushtrime-per-syte/rregulli-20-20-20): Çfarë është rregulli 20-20-20, çfarë është lodhja digjitale e syve, çfarë gjeti një studim i 2022 për pushimet nga ekrani dhe këshillat e AOA për ekranin.
- [Mitet për ushtrimet e syve: pëllëmbët, metoda Bates, syzet](https://ocufuse.com/sq/ushtrime-per-syte/mitet): A mund t'i zëvendësojnë syzet ushtrimet e syve? Çfarë thonë organizatat e kujdesit për sytë për mbulimin me pëllëmbë, metodën Bates dhe disleksinë.
- [Regjistri i ushtrimeve të syve: ndiq ushtrimet e përshkruara](https://ocufuse.com/sq/ushtrime-per-syte/regjistri-i-ushtrimeve): Çfarë të shënosh kur bën në shtëpi ushtrimet e përshkruara të syve, një format i thjeshtë regjistri dhe si ta çosh te ortoptisti ose optometristi.

## Blog
- [Is VR bad for your eyes?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/is-vr-bad-for-your-eyes): Eye doctors see no sign VR headsets harm the eyes, but long sessions can leave them tired and dry. Why that happens and what makes VR more comfortable.
- [Do I need to wear my glasses all the time?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/do-i-need-to-wear-my-glasses-all-the-time): Often not. Taking glasses off doesn't harm your eyes or change your prescription, and wearing them full time doesn't weaken your eyes. What decides it.
- [Do I need computer glasses, or are my progressives enough?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/do-i-need-computer-glasses): Glasses made for screen distance can help when everyday lenses make you tilt your head or lean in. What eye care groups say and what to ask at your exam.
- [How long does it take to adjust to new glasses?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-long-to-adjust-to-new-glasses): Usually a few days, sometimes up to two weeks, longer with progressives or a big change. What's normal, what helps and when to take them back.
- [Is an e-reader easier on the eyes than a tablet or phone?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/is-an-e-reader-easier-on-the-eyes): Studies comparing e-ink and LCD screens disagree, and setup matters as much as the device. What the research found and what eye care groups suggest.
- [Why is far away blurry after a long day at the computer?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/blurry-distance-vision-after-computer): Hours of close screen focus can leave distance vision a little blurry for a while. What eye care groups say about it and when to book an exam.
- [Why do my contacts feel dry when I work at a computer?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/contact-lenses-dry-at-the-computer): People blink about half as often at a screen, and a lens on a less wet eye dries out faster. What eye care groups suggest for long screen days.
- [Stretchly alternative: break reminders with an eye journal](https://ocufuse.com/blog/stretchly-alternative): Stretchly is a free, open source break reminder. When a browser timer or the Ocufuse web app may suit you better, and how they compare.
- [LookAway alternative for Windows, Chromebook or any browser](https://ocufuse.com/blog/lookaway-alternative): LookAway is a paid Mac break app. If you're on Windows, a Chromebook or a work laptop, here are alternatives, including a free 20-20-20 timer in your browser.
- [Best eye break apps: LookAway, Stretchly and free timers](https://ocufuse.com/blog/best-eye-break-apps): Four ways to get screen break reminders: LookAway for Mac, Stretchly for any computer, a free 20-20-20 timer in your browser and the Ocufuse focus timer.
- [Vision changes with age: what's common, what to check](https://ocufuse.com/blog/vision-changes-with-age): Reading glasses and slower adjustment to the dark are common with age. Changes eye care bodies describe, and how often to get checked.
- [How to put in eye drops: a step-by-step guide](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-to-put-in-eye-drops): The eye drop technique the American Academy of Ophthalmology describes, a lying-down method for nervous blinkers, and tips for children.
- [Eye safety at home: DIY, cleaning and the garden](https://ocufuse.com/blog/eye-safety-at-home): Nearly half of eye injuries happen at home. Everyday jobs that put eyes at risk, simple protective habits, and first steps after an injury.
- [Screen time and children's eyes: everyday habits](https://ocufuse.com/blog/screen-time-and-childrens-eyes): What eye care and pediatric bodies say about screens and children's eyes, and practical habits for breaks, distance, light and sleep.
- [How to read your glasses prescription](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-to-read-your-glasses-prescription): OD, OS, SPH, CYL, AXIS and ADD explained in plain words with a labelled example, and why a contact lens prescription is different.
- [What happens during an eye exam?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/what-happens-during-an-eye-exam): A step-by-step guide to a comprehensive eye exam: each test, what it checks, how long it takes, what dilation is like and how to prepare.
- [Why do eyes look red in flash photos?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/why-eyes-look-red-in-flash-photos): The red-eye effect is light reflected from the back of the eye. Why it happens, why some photos show it, and when a reflection needs a check.
- [The blind spot in your eye: why everyone has one](https://ocufuse.com/blog/the-blind-spot-in-your-eye): Every eye has a small spot that can't see. Where it is, why you never notice it, a quick way to find yours, and when a gap needs checking.
- [What does 20/20 vision mean?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/what-does-20-20-vision-mean): The two numbers in 20/20 and 20/40 explained, what 6/6 means, and the parts of your vision and eye health a letter chart doesn't measure.
- [Wildfire smoke and your eyes: what to do on smoky days](https://ocufuse.com/blog/wildfire-smoke-and-your-eyes): Smoke can leave eyes stinging, red and watery. What health and eye care bodies say, simple steps for smoky days, and when to get help.
- [Dry eyes in the morning: why they happen](https://ocufuse.com/blog/dry-eyes-in-the-morning): Waking with dry, scratchy or red eyes is common. Why eyes dry out overnight, bedroom changes that may help, and when to get an eye exam.
- [Tiny moving dots when you look at the sky: what they are](https://ocufuse.com/blog/moving-dots-when-you-look-at-the-sky): The tiny bright dots that dart about against a blue sky are white blood cells. What they are and how they differ from floaters and flashes.
- [Puffy eyes in the morning: common reasons](https://ocufuse.com/blog/puffy-eyes-in-the-morning): Swollen eyelids on waking are common. Why fluid gathers around the eyes overnight, habits that may help, and when swelling should be checked.
- [What to do on a screen break (that isn't another screen)](https://ocufuse.com/blog/what-to-do-on-a-screen-break): Swapping a laptop for a phone isn't much of a break. Simple things to do in 20 seconds, 5 minutes or 15 minutes away from the screen.
- [Gaming and your eyes: comfort habits for long sessions](https://ocufuse.com/blog/gaming-and-your-eyes): Long gaming sessions can leave eyes tired, dry and blurry. What an AOA survey found, and practical habits for distance, light and breaks.
- [Does using your phone in the dark damage your eyes?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/using-your-phone-in-the-dark): Scrolling in bed with the lights off won't damage your eyes, but it can tire them. What eye doctors say, and habits for screens at night.
- [How far should your monitor be from your eyes?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-far-should-your-monitor-be-from-your-eyes): About an arm's length, with the top of the screen at or just below eye level. The distances and angles OSHA, Mayo Clinic and eye care bodies suggest.
- [How to watch a solar eclipse safely](https://ocufuse.com/blog/watching-a-solar-eclipse-safely): Looking at the sun, even partly covered, can permanently damage the eyes. How to watch an eclipse with certified viewers or a pinhole.
- [How to put in contact lenses: steps for beginners](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-to-put-in-contact-lenses): The steps for putting in contact lenses, how to tell if a lens is inside out, and the hygiene habits that matter most.
- [Eye makeup and eye hygiene: everyday habits](https://ocufuse.com/blog/eye-makeup-and-eye-hygiene): Habits from the American Academy of Ophthalmology and the FDA for applying, storing and removing eye makeup safely.
- [When should a child have their first eye exam?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/when-should-a-child-have-an-eye-exam): When eye care bodies recommend checking children's eyes, how a screening differs from a full exam, and signs that shouldn't wait.
- [How to describe vision changes to your doctor](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-to-describe-vision-changes): Blurry can mean a dozen things. Words and details that help an eye care professional understand what you see, and how to note them.
- [Optometrist vs ophthalmologist vs optician](https://ocufuse.com/blog/optometrist-vs-ophthalmologist-vs-optician): Three similar names, three different jobs. Who does eye exams, who handles eye disease and surgery, who fits glasses, and who to see first.
- [Can your eye colour change?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/can-your-eye-color-change): Babies' eyes often darken, and light can change how eyes look. What sets eye colour, and why a real change in an adult's eye needs a check.
- [Why do pupils change size?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/why-pupils-change-size): Pupils shrink in bright light and widen in the dark. How the pupil reflex works, other everyday reasons, and when a change needs a doctor.
- [Nearsighted vs farsighted: what's the difference?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/nearsighted-vs-farsighted): Which one blurs distant things and which blurs close ones, why it happens, common signs, and how an eye exam checks and corrects each.
- [Swimming and your eyes: chlorine, goggles and contacts](https://ocufuse.com/blog/swimming-and-your-eyes): Red, stinging eyes after the pool are common. What chlorine does to the eye's surface, simple swim habits, and why contacts and water don't mix.
- [Dry eyes in winter: heating, wind and cold air](https://ocufuse.com/blog/dry-eyes-in-winter): Cold wind outside and heated air inside can both dry the eyes. Simple changes indoors and out, and when winter dryness needs an eye exam.
- [Crusty eyes in the morning: what sleep crust is](https://ocufuse.com/blog/crusty-eyes-in-the-morning): Sleep crust forms because you don't blink while asleep. What it's made of, how to clean it gently, and discharge that means a call to your doctor.
- [Blurry vision in the morning: why it happens](https://ocufuse.com/blog/blurry-vision-in-the-morning): Blur on waking that clears after a few blinks is common. Why the eye's surface can dry overnight, what to note, and when to get an eye exam.
- [Eye floaters: what they are and when to get help](https://ocufuse.com/blog/eye-floaters-what-they-are): Floaters are specks and threads that drift across your vision. What causes them, and the signs that mean you need an eye check the same day.
- [Can eye strain cause headaches?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/can-eye-strain-cause-headaches): Headache is a listed symptom of eye strain, but not every headache comes from the eyes. What to note, and which headaches need urgent help.
- [Is sitting close to the TV bad for your eyes?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/is-sitting-close-to-the-tv-bad-for-your-eyes): Sitting close to the TV doesn't damage the eyes, eye doctors say, but it can strain them. Why kids do it and when it's a sign to book an eye test.
- [Is dark mode better for your eyes?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/is-dark-mode-better-for-your-eyes): Neither mode suits everyone. What eye care and workplace bodies say about light and dark screens, and how to choose for the room you're in.
- [Night driving and glare: why it gets harder](https://ocufuse.com/blog/night-driving-glare): Headlight glare and slower adjustment to the dark make night driving harder for many people. Why, simple checks, and when to see a doctor.
- [Rubbing your eyes: why eye doctors say go gently](https://ocufuse.com/blog/rubbing-your-eyes): Rubbing tired or itchy eyes feels good for a moment. Why ophthalmologists advise against it, and gentler things to try instead.
- [Signs a child may have trouble seeing](https://ocufuse.com/blog/signs-a-child-may-have-trouble-seeing): Children rarely say they can't see well; they adapt. The everyday signs eye care bodies say parents and teachers can notice.
- [Your family eye health history: what to ask](https://ocufuse.com/blog/family-eye-health-history): Some eye conditions run in families. Which ones to ask relatives about, how to write it down, and why it can change how often you're checked.
- [How long does eye dilation last?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-long-does-eye-dilation-last): Dilating drops usually wear off within a few to several hours. What affects how long it lasts, what it feels like, and how to plan your day.
- [Eye myths and facts: what eye doctors say](https://ocufuse.com/blog/eye-myths-and-facts): Carrots, crossed eyes, glasses that weaken your eyes and screens that ruin them. What the American Academy of Ophthalmology says.
- [Colour blindness explained: types, causes and testing](https://ocufuse.com/blog/color-blindness-explained): Most people with colour blindness still see colour, just differently. What causes it, why it's more common in men, the types and testing.
- [What is astigmatism? A plain-language guide](https://ocufuse.com/blog/what-is-astigmatism): Astigmatism is one of the most common reasons for blurry vision. What it is, what it can feel like, and how an eye exam checks for it.
- [How the eye works: a simple guide to its parts](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-the-eye-works): From the cornea at the front to the optic nerve at the back: what each part of the eye does and how light becomes the image you see.
- [Dry eyes when flying: comfort tips for the cabin](https://ocufuse.com/blog/dry-eyes-when-flying): Cabin air dries the eyes on long flights. What to pack in your hand luggage, contact lens tips and in-flight habits from eye care bodies.
- [Eye allergies in pollen season: everyday habits](https://ocufuse.com/blog/eye-allergies-in-pollen-season): Itchy, watery, red eyes in spring and summer are often linked to pollen. Everyday habits from eye care bodies for high pollen days.
- [Feels like something is in your eye? Common reasons](https://ocufuse.com/blog/feels-like-something-in-your-eye): That gritty feeling isn't always grit. Common causes, first aid if something really is in your eye, and when the feeling needs an eye exam.
- [Why are my eyes watering? Common reasons](https://ocufuse.com/blog/why-are-my-eyes-watering): Wind, dry eyes, allergies and blocked tear ducts can all make eyes water. Common causes from the NHS and Mayo Clinic, and when to get help.
- [How often should you take a break from the computer?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-often-to-take-a-break-from-the-computer): Short and often beats long and rare. What workplace and eye care guidance says about screen breaks, with an example hour.
- [Screen glare and brightness: setting up light at your desk](https://ocufuse.com/blog/screen-glare-and-brightness-at-your-desk): Reflections and a screen brighter than the room tire the eyes. Simple layout and brightness changes that workplace and eye care bodies suggest.
- [How often do you blink, and why do screens change it?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-often-do-you-blink): Most adults blink about 15 times a minute, far less at a screen. What blinking does, what research found about screens, and simple habits.
- [Sunglasses UV ratings: what the labels mean](https://ocufuse.com/blog/sunglasses-and-uv-choosing-a-pair): What UV400, 100% UV protection and lens categories 0 to 4 mean on sunglasses, and why a darker or pricier lens doesn't mean more UV protection.
- [Reading glasses after 40: what presbyopia is](https://ocufuse.com/blog/reading-glasses-after-40-presbyopia): Holding your phone further away to read it is one of the most common changes in midlife. What presbyopia is, why it happens, and the options an eye care professional may discuss.
- [Myopia in children: why time outdoors matters](https://ocufuse.com/blog/myopia-in-children-time-outdoors): Short-sightedness is becoming more common in children. What a large school trial found about outdoor time, and simple ways to fit more of it into the week.
- [How often should you get your eyes checked?](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-often-should-you-get-your-eyes-checked): Many eye conditions don't cause symptoms early on. What UK and US eye care bodies recommend for routine eye tests, and who may need to go more often.
- [Contact lens habits that lower infection risk](https://ocufuse.com/blog/contact-lens-habits-infection-risk): Most contact lens wearers have at least one risky habit. The everyday steps eye care bodies recommend, from sleeping and water to cases and solution.
- [Dry eyes at work: small changes to your desk and day](https://ocufuse.com/blog/dry-eyes-at-work-desk-and-day): Air conditioning, screens and long meetings can leave eyes dry and gritty by the afternoon. Practical changes to your workspace and routine, and when dryness needs a professional.
- [Do blue light glasses help? What the research says](https://ocufuse.com/blog/do-blue-light-glasses-help): Blue light glasses are sold for eye strain, sleep and eye protection. A 2023 Cochrane review looked at the trials. Here is what the evidence does and doesn't show.
- [The 20-20-20 rule: what a 2023 study actually found](https://ocufuse.com/blog/20-20-20-rule-what-the-research-found): The 20-20-20 rule is one of the most repeated pieces of screen advice. A small study tested it with break reminders. Here is what changed, what didn't, and what it means for your day.
- [Diabetes and your eyes: why yearly screening matters](https://ocufuse.com/blog/diabetes-and-your-eyes-yearly-screening): Diabetes can affect the eyes long before you notice any change in your sight. Why regular eye checks are recommended, what screening involves, and how to prepare.
- [Sleep, screens and tired eyes](https://ocufuse.com/blog/sleep-screens-and-tired-eyes): Late-night scrolling, short sleep and tired eyes often go together. What studies say about screens before bed, and how to spot your own pattern.
- [How to photograph your child's eyes for a doctor](https://ocufuse.com/blog/photographing-your-childs-eyes-for-the-eye-doctor): An eye that sometimes turns in or out often behaves perfectly at the appointment. How to capture useful photos and short videos of a child's eyes at home.
- [Red eye: when to watch it and when to see a doctor](https://ocufuse.com/blog/red-eye-when-to-see-a-doctor): Many red eyes are minor, but some need care the same day. The signs that separate the two, and what to note while you wait for an appointment.
- [Screen eye strain: causes, habits and when to get checked](https://ocufuse.com/blog/screen-eye-strain-what-helps): Tired, dry or blurry eyes after screen time? The habits with the best evidence, what blue light glasses really do, and when to get your eyes checked.
- [Double vision that comes and goes: what to note](https://ocufuse.com/blog/double-vision-that-comes-and-goes): If you sometimes see double, a few simple observations make your doctor's job easier. What to check, what to write down, and when double vision is an emergency.
- [Drooping eyelid: what to record and when it's urgent](https://ocufuse.com/blog/drooping-eyelid-what-to-record): When one eyelid sits lower than before, consistent photos help your doctor. How to take them, what to note, and the warning signs that cannot wait.
- [What to tell your eye doctor: symptoms, history, questions](https://ocufuse.com/blog/what-to-tell-your-eye-doctor): Eye appointments are short. What to bring, what to describe and which questions to ask, so the things you meant to mention don't get forgotten.
- [Dry eye diary: a simple format your doctor can use](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-to-keep-a-dry-eye-diary): Dry, gritty or watery eyes often depend on the day. A simple diary format that shows the pattern, plus what to bring to your appointment.
- [Eye twitching that won't stop: causes and notes](https://ocufuse.com/blog/eye-twitching-that-wont-stop): A twitching eyelid is common and usually settles on its own. What tends to set it off, what to write down, and when it is worth getting checked.
- [Why your eye photos look different day to day](https://ocufuse.com/blog/why-eye-photos-look-different-day-to-day): Two photos of the same eyes can look surprisingly different. The everyday reasons why, from light to camera angle, and what they do and don't tell you.
- [Eye symptoms that come and go: preparing for your visit](https://ocufuse.com/blog/preparing-for-an-eye-appointment-when-symptoms-come-and-go): Some eye symptoms disappear right before the appointment. How to keep a simple record so your doctor can see what happens on the other days.
- [How to take consistent eye photos at home](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-to-take-consistent-eye-photos): Light, distance and angle change how your eyes look in a photo. Six habits that make daily eye photos comparable from one day to the next.
